sentence_stem: Had she accepted the job offer last year,
correct_completion: she would be living abroad by now.
full_sentence: Had she accepted the job offer last year, she would be living abroad by now.
acceptable_variants: she would now be living overseas.
she would be living a very different life today.

options.why_wrong: The simple present does not express an unreal result of a past condition. The result clause needs 'would' plus a base verb.

options.text: she would have lived abroad last year.
options.why_wrong: The perfect form points to the past, which conflicts with 'by now'. Mixed conditionals link a past condition to a present result.

options.text: she would be living abroad by now.
she will live abroad next year.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' expresses a real future plan, not an unreal result of a past condition. The sentence needs 'would' here.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals with inverted 'had' (past condition, present result)
explanation: 'Had she accepted' is an inverted form of 'If she had accepted', which is a mixed conditional. The past condition is followed by a present-time result built with 'would' plus a base verb. Turkish speakers may find the inverted 'had' word order unfamiliar because Turkish conditionals are formed with a suffix, so the subject-verb inversion is easy to overlook.
